title: Value vs Reference Types in C#

scenes.line1: Why do structs and classes behave
scenes.say: Ever wonder why structs and classes in C sharp act so differently? Let's break down value and reference types.

scenes.label: Value
scenes.sub: Structs store data directly. Copies make new, independent values.
scenes.say: Structs are value types. They store data directly, and copying them creates a new, independent value.

scenes.label: Reference
scenes.sub: Classes store references to data on the heap.
scenes.say: Classes are reference types. They store a reference to data on the heap. Assigning a class just copies the reference, not the data.
When you assign a value type like an int to an object, C sharp copies it to the heap. This is called boxing.
Records are reference types, but they compare by value. That means two records with the same data are equal.

scenes.question: Are structs nullable by default?
scenes.right: No. Only reference types are nullable by default. Use Nullable<T> for structs.
scenes.say: Here's a common interview trap: Are structs nullable by default? No. Only reference types are. Use Nullable of T for structs.
